The negative control demonstrates it removes exactly the three AttributeError failures, and the double carries the locator as the production Null1D type so a type drift would surface. It is not a new guard, and a future addition to the geometry-identity inputs would require extending the double, which is the same brittleness the production fixture has.
justifications.evidence: The head gate is recorded and independently reproduced (5 passed both in the recorded default import mode run from the reviewed worktree and in an importlib-mode run over the absolute path), and the negative control records the base revision's 3 failed / 2 passed with the same AttributeError at forward_operator.py:2599. justifications.fit: Both commits use a conventional subject with a body stating why, no plan or ticket identifiers appear, and the evidence fragment follows the standard evidence-doc head with project/plan meta. The repair reuses the existing fixture through a module-symbol monkeypatch rather than duplicating operator construction.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The change does precisely what the assigned repair requires: it carries the stationary-point locator and the operator area entry the geometry identity reads onto the request-seam doubles, and nothing more. Verified against the live product that reads them: ForwardFluxOperator._compute_geometry_identity consumes self.grid.null, self.wall.null and self.area (nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py:2599).
justifications.reuse: No new machinery is introduced: a single small double and one helper reuse the existing shared linear fixture, and the double is registered as a pytree so the existing traced solve path carries it without a parallel code path.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exactly two granted paths changed, no product source touched, and the three residual failures that the concurrent cfs-policy-tuple node owns are reported as a scope note rather than triaged outside the write fence; the scratch-copy baseline recording is the only reconciliation blemish and is reported as a follow-on.

limitations: The baseline arm ran a renamed scratch copy (test_forward_solve_request_base.py), so its node ids do not reconcile id-for-id with the head arm's; no false added-failure count arises because the head arm records no failures.

The _completed_profile helper sets several geometry-identity inputs (cell_average_stencil, cell_average_weight, inside_material, moment_geometry, wall_unit_*) to None placeholders, so the geometry-identity digest computed in these tests is not a faithful digest; this is acceptable for request-seam tests that assert request/receipt behaviour, not identity content.
